scope: Correctness and cleanup, not a timing benchmark or C/Rust comparison. The fixture runs 64 rounds and compares raw interpretation with native ARC/tracing at O0/O2, and ARC WebAssembly at O1/O2. It covers callbacks owning locally created data queues, nested queues, records/lists, empty captures, aliases, repeated calls, undrained/closed queues, errors, blocked sends and cancellation. Unknown/native queue sources and function-bearing captured queues remain rejected. Default tracing is unchanged.
native_measurements: Generated-C counters require no more than 64 simultaneously live queue objects, at least one created queue, and zero remaining at teardown. ARC additionally requires full repayment of managed allocator charges and zero tracing collections. These measurements exclude external allocations, do not count retain/release operations and are not a total-process memory bound. Native tracing runs enable stress, collection verification and reuse verification.
native_control: Omitting the release of a queued value must exceed the live-queue bound and exit 198 in ARC at both optimization levels. Actual native disassembly excludes collector scan/mark/sweep routines in ARC; tracing controls retain marking.
wasm_measurements: Both Linux hosts run Node 24. WASI and the browser loader each run JSPI and Asyncify, at O1/O2. Each combination runs ordinary, allocation-instrumented, omitted-scheduler-shutdown and omitted-queue-release modules. Ordinary/measured modules return 0; both omission controls must return 244. Instrumented checks compare physical allocations, bytes and count-table entries with the entry baseline. This verifies the browser loader under Node, not an actual browser engine. Module headers, saved C, output and successful-run symbol listings are inspected; no independent local WebAssembly disassembly is claimed.
